determinism: The cases come from `seed` and `generator_count`. Dict keys are sorted, the case order is the generation order (an id is the ordinal), and the file is ASCII: every code point outside ASCII is a \uXXXX escape, so a parser cannot read this file two ways.

forms.cut: SHA-256 of the body a text leaf is hashed with — the strict form of the text cut to the §2 size limit in code points — UTF-8, base64
forms.free: SHA-256 of the free text form of the text (canonical-content.md §2b), UTF-8, base64
forms.html: SHA-256 of the text left after the §6.1 removal, UTF-8, base64
forms.manifest: the `k` of each leaf, in order, joined with `|`
forms.strict: SHA-256 of the strict form of the text (canonical-content.md §2), UTF-8, base64

bytes.asks: canonical-content.md §2 step 0 (read the bytes to text with the declared charset), and then §2 and §2b over the text that was read, so a reading that differs shows up as a hash that differs, exactly as it would in a message

cut.asks: canonical-content.md §2 including the "Body Size Limit": the text is normalised and then cut to the first 1 048 576 CODE POINTS — not the first 1 048 576 UTF-16 code units, which is a different body whenever the code point in front of the cut is outside the BMP. The answer is the hash of the body a text leaf would be hashed with, so a cut that differs by one code point differs as a hash
cut.input: `parts`: the body as a RECIPE — pieces of the form `{"literal": "s"}` and `{"repeat": "s", "count": n}`, joined in order. `value` says the same recipe in words. A body over the §2 limit is a megabyte and is not written out in this file

html.asks: canonical-content.md §2b over an HTML part. The strict form is not asked: it hashes the HTML source, which the vector files pin already
html.input: `text`: the source of an HTML part

html-envelope.asks: delivered-envelope.md §6.1 (take the block off), then canonical-content.md §2b over the text that is left. Both are asked, because the free text form flattens markup and on its own would hide a block that was left behind
html-envelope.input: `text`: a DELIVERED HTML part, with a signer's block in it

manifest.asks: canonical-content.md §9.1 (the walk) and §9.2a (the one reading of a boundary parameter). The answer is a STRUCTURE, not a hash: the `k` of each leaf the walk finds, in order, joined with `|`. A reader that cannot read the message at all answers `error:<exception class>`

subject.asks: canonical-content.md §5 (RFC 2047 encoded words), and then §2 and §2b over the text that was read
subject.input: `value`: a Subject field as it arrives

text.asks: canonical-content.md §2 (the strict form) and §2b (the free text form)
text.input: `text`: the text of a plain part

reference_implementation.note: The same code, called the same way, that the project's own cross-implementation comparison uses for its Python reader.
